k: Mercy Vale. I gave her a nod every morning at this gate. She'd bless my boots.
src: 'Mercy Vale. I gave her a nod every morning at this gate. She\'d bless my boots.'

k: I've thrown the boots in the river.
src: 'I\'ve thrown the boots in the river.'

k: Heading south? The Pilgrim Road runs straight to the Sunscar. Take water.
src: 'Heading south? The Pilgrim Road runs straight to the Sunscar. Take water.'

k: Take more water than that.
src: 'Take more water than that.'

k: HEAR YE! His Holiness the Hierophant returns from the western isles! The Grand Lantern burns bright!
src: 'HEAR YE! His Holiness the Hierophant returns from the western isles! The Grand Lantern burns bright!'

k: Also bread is up a copper!
src: 'Also bread is up a copper!'

k: HEAR YE! The Choir reminds all citizens that the Undercroft is CLOSED and CONDEMNED and NOT A PLACE FOR CHILDREN!
src: 'HEAR YE! The Choir reminds all citizens that the Undercroft is CLOSED and CONDEMNED and NOT A PLACE FOR CHILDREN!'

k: Also bread is up another copper!
src: 'Also bread is up another copper!'

k: HEAR YE! Sister Mercy Vale is CAST OUT of the Choir! A reward for information on her whereabouts!
src: 'HEAR YE! Sister Mercy Vale is CAST OUT of the Choir! A reward for information on her whereabouts!'

k: And bread is DOWN a copper, by order of the Hierophant! Long live the Hierophant!
src: 'And bread is DOWN a copper, by order of the Hierophant! Long live the Hierophant!'

k: River's low. The Aure's never this low in autumn.
src: 'River\'s low. The Aure\'s never this low in autumn.'

k: The old bargemen say the sea's pulling at it, way out west. Like it's holding its breath.
src: 'The old bargemen say the sea\'s pulling at it, way out west. Like it\'s holding its breath.'

k: Hettie says I'm to rest. I'm resting standing up. It's a baker's skill.
src: 'Hettie says I\'m to rest. I\'m resting standing up. It\'s a baker\'s skill.'

k: I dream about the singing, sometimes. Then I wake up and there's bread to make. It helps, the bread.
src: 'I dream about the singing, sometimes. Then I wake up and there\'s bread to make. It helps, the bread.'

k: Saltglass pepper! Sunscar cumin! Dried figs from the caravan roads!
src: 'Saltglass pepper! Sunscar cumin! Dried figs from the caravan roads!'

k: The Keeper down south, Tamsin — blind as a stone, they say, and sees more than you or me. She told my caravan-master the day he'd die.
src: 'The Keeper down south, Tamsin — blind as a stone, they say, and sees more than you or me. She told my caravan-master the day he\'d die.'

k: He's been avoiding that day ever since. Very successfully.
src: 'He\'s been avoiding that day ever since. Very successfully.'

k: South? To Saltglass? Give Keeper Tamsin my regards.
src: 'South? To Saltglass? Give Keeper Tamsin my regards.'

k: ...Actually, don't. She'll know exactly who I am.
src: '...Actually, don\'t. She\'ll know exactly who I am.'

k: Behold! Fenwick the Fabulous juggles THREE bells—
src: 'Behold! Fenwick the Fabulous juggles THREE bells—'

k: _(CLANG)_
src: '_(CLANG)_'

k: —two bells. Behold! Two bells.
src: '—two bells. Behold! Two bells.'

k: A new act, in honor of the brave children of the Undercroft! I shall juggle FOUR bells!
src: 'A new act, in honor of the brave children of the Undercroft! I shall juggle FOUR bells!'

k: _(CLANG) (CLANG)_
src: '_(CLANG) (CLANG)_'

k: In honor of the brave children, I shall juggle two bells.
src: 'In honor of the brave children, I shall juggle two bells.'

k: Did you see the Hierophant's ship come in? The _Aubade._ White as milk, sails like folded wings.
src: 'Did you see the Hierophant\'s ship come in? The _Aubade._ White as milk, sails like folded wings.'

k: Fastest ship in the world. Lucky for him. Some of us walk.
src: 'Fastest ship in the world. Lucky for him. Some of us walk.'

k: Fourteen people brought up out of the Undercroft! They say a girl from the islands led them. The Hierophant's own Page!
src: 'Fourteen people brought up out of the Undercroft! They say a girl from the islands led them. The Hierophant\'s own Page!'

k: ...Wait. Is that—
src: '...Wait. Is that—'

k: The Bell Market's been here six hundred years. Prices have been going up for five hundred and ninety-nine of them.
src: 'The Bell Market\'s been here six hundred years. Prices have been going up for five hundred and ninety-nine of them.'

k: The first year was lovely, they say.
src: 'The first year was lovely, they say.'

k: Forty years ago this autumn, the Lantern went out for one night. I was nine.
src: 'Forty years ago this autumn, the Lantern went out for one night. I was nine.'

k: My mother held her hand over my eyes until dawn. I've come every day since to thank it. For coming back.
src: 'My mother held her hand over my eyes until dawn. I\'ve come every day since to thank it. For coming back.'

k: Some didn't come back, that night. Three hundred and twelve, they say. The Keeper's own daughter among them.
src: 'Some didn\'t come back, that night. Three hundred and twelve, they say. The Keeper\'s own daughter among them.'

k: The Hierophant was her brother, you know. Twelve years old. He saw it all.
src: 'The Hierophant was her brother, you know. Twelve years old. He saw it all.'

k: The Grand Lantern is open to the Choir only, citizen.
src: 'The Grand Lantern is open to the Choir only, citizen.'

k: Admire it from there. It's very admirable from there.
src: 'Admire it from there. It\'s very admirable from there.'

k: Eyes front. No touching the Lantern. No singing at the Lantern. No proposing marriage at the Lantern — we've had a spate.
src: 'Eyes front. No touching the Lantern. No singing at the Lantern. No proposing marriage at the Lantern — we\'ve had a spate.'

k: The Lord-Commander's doubled the watch. Every Sister of Small Mercies is under guard.
src: 'The Lord-Commander\'s doubled the watch. Every Sister of Small Mercies is under guard.'

k: They just sit in the almshouse and sing. Quietly. All day. I've asked for a transfer.
src: 'They just sit in the almshouse and sing. Quietly. All day. I\'ve asked for a transfer.'

k: The dawn-office is at first bell. The noon-office at noon. The dusk-office... you can see where this is going.
src: 'The dawn-office is at first bell. The noon-office at noon. The dusk-office... you can see where this is going.'

k: We've been told not to speak of Sister Mercy. So I won't.
src: 'We\'ve been told not to speak of Sister Mercy. So I won\'t.'

k: ...She taught me my letters. When I was small. She was so patient.
src: '...She taught me my letters. When I was small. She was so patient.'

k: I walked from Mirefen to see the Grand Lantern. Three weeks. My feet are a disgrace.
src: 'I walked from Mirefen to see the Grand Lantern. Three weeks. My feet are a disgrace.'

k: There's a sickness in the swamp. Mother Osk says it's the Gloam, getting into the water. Nobody listens to Mother Osk.
src: 'There\'s a sickness in the swamp. Mother Osk says it\'s the Gloam, getting into the water. Nobody listens to Mother Osk.'

k: Then again, she's usually right.
src: 'Then again, she\'s usually right.'

k: Lantern resonance! The Seven Lanterns sing at seven _slightly_ different pitches. A sloppiness I find personally offensive.
src: 'Lantern resonance! The Seven Lanterns sing at seven _slightly_ different pitches. A sloppiness I find personally offensive.'

k: Brother Halvard of Frosthollow wrote a monograph on it. Wrong, mostly. Elegantly wrong.
src: 'Brother Halvard of Frosthollow wrote a monograph on it. Wrong, mostly. Elegantly wrong.'

k: Tuning forks, to bring the Lanterns into harmony? ...Fascinating.
src: 'Tuning forks, to bring the Lanterns into harmony? ...Fascinating.'

k: Dangerous, if it were done wrong, of course. A Lantern tuned to the wrong note would — well. Everything worth doing is dangerous.
src: 'Dangerous, if it were done wrong, of course. A Lantern tuned to the wrong note would — well. Everything worth doing is dangerous.'

k: My Kindling's next spring. Father says I'll be an Arcanist, because Father was an Arcanist, and Father's father.
src: 'My Kindling\'s next spring. Father says I\'ll be an Arcanist, because Father was an Arcanist, and Father\'s father.'

k: I want to be a Ranger. ...Don't tell Father.
src: 'I want to be a Ranger. ...Don\'t tell Father.'

k: Is that a _street kid?_ Father says street kids bite.
src: 'Is that a _street kid?_ Father says street kids bite.'

k: Only on Tuesdays.
src: 'Only on Tuesdays.'

k: ...Is it Tuesday?
src: '...Is it Tuesday?'

k: Did you hear? The Hierophant has taken a Page. Some girl from the islands. _Fishing_ people.
src: 'Did you hear? The Hierophant has taken a Page. Some girl from the islands. _Fishing_ people.'

k: Can you imagine? Smelling of mackerel, in the Cathedral.
src: 'Can you imagine? Smelling of mackerel, in the Cathedral.'

k: I always said that Mercy woman smiled too much.
src: 'I always said that Mercy woman smiled too much.'

k: I never said it _out loud_, you understand. But I always said it.
src: 'I never said it _out loud_, you understand. But I always said it.'

k: Pip! Haven't seen you since you nicked my good boot.
src: 'Pip! Haven\'t seen you since you nicked my good boot.'

k: You had two.
src: 'You had two.'

k: I _had_ two.
src: 'I _had_ two.'

k: Rag and bone! Bone trade's back to normal, thank the dawn. Somebody'd been buying up every bone in Low Town.
src: 'Rag and bone! Bone trade\'s back to normal, thank the dawn. Somebody\'d been buying up every bone in Low Town.'

k: Now I know who, I'd rather not have sold 'em.
src: 'Now I know who, I\'d rather not have sold \'em.'

k: Rag and bone! ...Mostly rag, lately. The bone trade's gone strange.
src: 'Rag and bone! ...Mostly rag, lately. The bone trade\'s gone strange.'

k: Somebody's been buying up all the bone in Low Town. Paying in soup.
src: 'Somebody\'s been buying up all the bone in Low Town. Paying in soup.'

k: Hic. The sh-sisters sing so pretty. Sing you right to sleep.
src: 'Hic. The sh-sisters sing so pretty. Sing you right to sleep.'

k: Sing you right to... where'd everyone go?
src: 'Sing you right to... where\'d everyone go?'

k: I've given up the drink. And the soup. Especially the soup.
src: 'I\'ve given up the drink. And the soup. Especially the soup.'

k: My Jory's fine. My Jory's at home. I keep checking.
src: 'My Jory\'s fine. My Jory\'s at home. I keep checking.'

k: Jory's still home. Thank the dawn. But Nell — oh, that poor scrap. She mended my washing-line for a bun, last week.
src: 'Jory\'s still home. Thank the dawn. But Nell — oh, that poor scrap. She mended my washing-line for a bun, last week.'

k: Jory wants to be a Dawnguard now. Or a Lantern Page. Or both. He's practicing on the cat.
src: 'Jory wants to be a Dawnguard now. Or a Lantern Page. Or both. He\'s practicing on the cat.'

k: Thank you for that. I think.
src: 'Thank you for that. I think.'

k: You're Pip's new friends? Did he steal you?
src: 'You\'re Pip\'s new friends? Did he steal you?'

k: He says he'll find Tuck and Wick. He says it every night.
src: 'He says he\'ll find Tuck and Wick. He says it every night.'

k: I pretend I believe him, so he can sleep.
src: 'I pretend I believe him, so he can sleep.'

k: Soup at noon and vespers. Beds for any who ask. Sister Mercy says no one should ever have to be cold.
src: 'Soup at noon and vespers. Beds for any who ask. Sister Mercy says no one should ever have to be cold.'
